messages.subject: Small Area Estimation (SAE) in INLA
parts:
I have data at 30 subnational units across 30 years. Each region has a  single point of information in each year.

I am running a SAE model in INLA to account for spatial relatedness and temporal correlation. 

However, when I plot the  the mean output per region year in one image they all have the same shape over time but different values. 

In the input data, the 30 curves shows a mixture of  shapes as expected since the profile of the outcome is different in each region. 

What I am doing wrong such that the shapes of the mean of the outcome exhibits similar shapes in time?

formula1<-y ~ 1 +
f(region.struct,model="besag",graph="nc.adj",hyper = list(prec = list(prior="loggamma",param=c(1,0.001))))+
f(region,model="iid")+
f(time.struct,model="rw1", hyper = list(prec = list(prior="pc.prec",param=c(0.33,0.01))))+
f(Time,model="iid")

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Small Area Estimation (SAE) in INLA
parts:
Hi,
you have constructed a separable model of the type u(s) + v(t), where
u(s) is a spatial function and v(t) is a temporal function, so the
effect you see is imposed by the model.

For temporally varying patterns you need a fully spatiotemporal
component, w(s,t).
The f(space,..., group=time, control.group=list(model="ar1", ...))
type of model provides this.
Look for the case studies and tutorial documents on r-inla.org for examples.

Finn
